title: Explains what src/main.rs does and reads it to confirm.
notes:
Read standalone, with no sibling chat store. The transcript records no timestamps, no model and no workspace, so all three read as absent rather than as an mtime or an inverted directory slug; the title falls back to the writer's own overview line. With the chat store present (see cursor_agent_chat_store) the title, started_at and model_name come from its meta row instead.

TOOL RESULTS: has_tool_results is false, and it is false for every cursor-agent transcript — but for a reason worth writing down, because nothing else tells a user why a converted cursor-agent session shows tool calls whose results are missing. The format has two writers and they disagree. The local writer (7923.index.js `I()`) builds each line's content from text, thinking and toolCalls only; the toolResult its own `M()` computes is never turned into a block, so a locally-run cursor-agent session loses ALL tool output before it ever reaches the file — a whole-format loss, not a per-field one. The cloud exporter (`cursor-agent cloud transcript <id>`, 6363.index.js `p()`) does carry tool output, but flattens it into a plain {type:'text'} block whose text is JSON.stringify({tool_call_id, tool_name, tool_args, tool_result}, null, 2) — which is what line 4 of this fixture is. Either way casr never populates tool_results: there is no tool_result block type to parse, so the cloud form arrives as ordinary message text on a Tool-role message and the structure is gone. Hence tool_call.result in known_lossy_fields.

The role:'tool' line is real vendor output, not an invention — but only the cloud exporter writes one. Both writers emit to the same path (<dataDir>/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/<id>/<id>.jsonl), so a reader must accept it.
